1.title: Clinical text embedding, endpoint prediction, and manuscript analysis workflow.
1.text: (a) Clinician notes, imaging reports, and pathology reports recorded before first treatment are encoded with Clinical ModernBERT. Mean token pooling produces 768 features per note. Recency-weighted pooling within each note type (lambda = 0.01 per day) and concatenation produce 2,304 patient-level text features; all three note types are required. First treatment defines baseline time zero. (b) Endpoint-specific elastic-net Cox models include text features, age, sex, cancer type, and note-era covariates. Patient partitions separate training and tuning from held-out evaluation for mortality/metastasis, ICD-10, and PhecodeX endpoints. (c) Main analyses evaluate clinical-text discrimination and survival stratification, compare published prognostic scores with text and their combination, compare clinical and genomic modalities, and characterize longitudinal mortality-risk trajectories using a fixed mortality model. The workflow is schematic; note marks, embeddings, score matrices, and mini-plots are illustrative. Cohort eligibility, data availability, and cancer-type and stage distributions are in Supplementary Table 1; endpoint counts are in Supplementary Table 2.

2.title: Discrimination and survival stratification using clinical text.
2.text: (a) Held-out Harrell's concordance index (C-index) for the base model, containing age, sex, and cancer type, versus the model additionally incorporating clinical-text embeddings. Each point represents an endpoint; the diagonal indicates equal discrimination. (b) Endpoint-level differences in C-index (text minus base), grouped by outcome scheme. Positive values favor the text model. Diamonds and bars indicate the median and interquartile range; violin densities are omitted for groups with fewer than ten endpoints. Endpoint counts are shown above each group. Endpoints are correlated, so these summaries are descriptive. (c,d) Kaplan-Meier estimates of overall survival from first treatment in the known-stage cohort, stratified by major cancer stage (c) or quartiles of the text-derived mortality-risk score (d). Quartiles are defined across this cohort, with Q1 the lowest and Q4 the highest risk. Shading denotes pointwise 95% confidence intervals. Displayed C-indices describe the corresponding stage or risk-score predictor. P values in c and d are from log-rank tests. (e) Overall-survival C-index for the published score alone, text alone, and their combination, with 95% patient-bootstrap confidence intervals, for mGPS, RMH, LIPI, ALBI, MELD, IPI, IMDC and MSKCC with ECOG, ECOG, and KPS. ECOG-free variants and CAPRA are excluded. The primary treatment-anchor, 30-day laboratory-window analysis is shown; score/source cohorts require at least 50 evaluated patients. Calculated scores and scores documented in notes are labeled separately, with evaluated patients and deaths. Full IMDC and MSKCC include the performance-status item (documented ECOG or KPS converted to ECOG); their ECOG-free variants are excluded. Each comparison uses the same patients and comparable pairs within text-model outer folds; the combined model cross-fits a Cox model on the published and text scores. Missing model estimates are marked as unavailable. ICD-10, International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision.

3.title: Relative predictive performance and joint associations across data modalities.
3.text: (a) Points indicate mean within-endpoint C-index ranks (1 = best); horizontal bars indicate interquartile ranges across endpoints. Ranking requires complete modality-performance results and is restricted to endpoints represented in the joint Cox analysis; its endpoint count may therefore be smaller than in the other panels. (b) Numbers of endpoints with a significant modality coefficient in the unpenalized joint Cox model. Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment is applied across modalities within each endpoint; significance is defined as false discovery rate below 0.05. (c) Distributions of joint Cox coefficients per one-standard-deviation increase in each modality's risk score. Positive coefficients indicate higher hazard conditional on the other modality scores. Points represent endpoints; diamonds and bars indicate the median and interquartile range. For display in c, coefficients outside 1.5 interquartile ranges of the first and third quartiles are omitted separately for each modality. Panels b and c use the same joint-model endpoint set before display trimming. Endpoints are correlated; summaries across endpoints are descriptive. PRS, polygenic risk scores; met. burden, metastatic burden.

4.title: Mortality-risk dynamics and survival across cancer stages.
4.text: (a) Longitudinal text-derived mortality-risk scores standardized within each observation month; colors are truncated at z = -2.5 and +2.5. Rows represent patients and columns represent months. Up to 500 patients per dynamics group are displayed, with shown/full cohort sizes labeled. Falling, stable, and rising groups are ordered by mean fitted risk-score slope. (b) Kaplan-Meier overall survival by dynamics group, conditional on survival to the indicated landmark. (c) Dynamics-group proportions among patients with each recognized stage and an assigned group. (d) Conditional overall survival for stage I-II patients with rising risk versus stage IV patients with falling risk. Legend counts in d report patients in each comparison group after landmark eligibility filtering. In b and d, shading denotes pointwise 95% confidence intervals; survival estimates use delayed entry at the landmark. Panel denominators differ with trajectory, survival, and stage-data availability.

S1.title: Eligible oncology cohort, data availability, and prediction endpoints.
S1.text: (a) Cumulative cohort selection beginning with the eligible oncology cohort as successive data-availability criteria are applied; each box is a subset of the preceding box. Repeated counts indicate criteria without additional attrition. PRS, polygenic risk scores; somatic, somatic genomic features. (b) Numbers of available prediction endpoints in the mortality/metastasis, three-character ICD-10, four-character ICD-10, and PhecodeX schemes. Endpoint counts are not patient counts, and related endpoints across coding schemes are not mutually exclusive. ICD-10, International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision.

S21.title: Cancer-type and stage distributions in the clinical-text cohort.
S21.text: (a) Cancer-type distribution among patients with cancer-type annotations and clinical text; counts and percentages use the same cohort denominator. Other combines less frequent cancer types for display. (b) Major cancer-stage distribution among patients with a recognized stage (I-IV). Panel-specific cohort denominators are shown in the artwork. These distributions were formerly Figure 1b and c.
